{{Use mdy dates|date=March 2024}}

'''Eric T. Kool''' (born 1960<ref name=H1C>{{Cite web |title=Eric Kool |url=https://archive.connect.h1.co/member/595308752375186/ |website=H1 Connect}}</ref>) is an American chemist, focusing in chemistry of RNA and DNA; probe design and imaging; synthetic biology, currently the George A. and Hilda M. Daubert Professor in Chemistry at [[Stanford University]] and is an Elected Fellow at the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.aaas.org/fellow/kool-eric |title=Eric Kool |publisher=aaas.org |accessdate=May 12, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://chemistry.stanford.edu/people/eric-kool |title=Eric Kool |publisher=stanford.edu |accessdate=May 12, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=gxFj6bAAAAAJ&hl=en |title=Eric T. Kool|accessdate=May 12, 2017}}</ref> 

Kool was born in [[Libertyville, Illinois]], and carried out undergraduate studies at [[Miami University]].<ref name=H1C /> He received the [[Beckman Young Investigators Award]] in 1992.<ref name=Beckman>{{cite web |title=Eric T. Kool |url=http://www.beckman-foundation.org/beckman-young-investigators/eric-t-kool |website=Arnold and Mabel Beckman Foundation |accessdate=1 August 2018}}</ref> He is the 2019 recipient of the [[Murray Goodman Memorial Prize]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Murray Goodman Memorial Prize 2019|date=29 October 2019 |url=https://www.advancedsciencenews.com/biopolymers-murray-goodman-memorial-prize-2019-eric-t-kool/}}</ref>
